thread.title: The Earnings Beat: Four Stocks To Watch For the Coming Week

author: Richard Saintvilus
title: The Earnings Beat: Four Stocks To Watch For the Coming Week
text:
Shutterstock photo It was another wild week in the stock market, during which the Dow Jones Industrial Average suffered not one, but two separate days of one-thousand point declines. We witnessed more aggressive selling in equities across all sectors, suggesting this wasn’t the typical rotation we’ve been accustomed to during this decade-long bull run.
Nevertheless, opportunities to buy quality high-growth companies, notably, the FAANGs, where Facebook ( FB ), Apple ( AAPL ), Amazon ( AMZN ), Netflix ( NFLX ) and Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ) combined lost more than $90 billion in market cap, don’t come often. "It is a course correction, not a panic sell-off," according to J.P. Morgan strategist David Kelly. Still Kelly added that "It's a reminder to people there's no such thing as a free lunch in the stock market.”
In other words, you have to pay to play. Investors who have been sitting on cash and can stomach the volatility should be encourage by the recent corporate earnings reported thus far. And as long as the earnings trend remains positive, the long-term trajectory of stocks will remain favorable. In that vein, here are five stocks to keep an eye on for this coming week.
Blue Apron ( APRN ) - Reports before the open, Tuesday, Feb. 13.
Wall Street expects a loss of 27 cents per share on revenue of $185.09 million. There company went public last spring, thus there are no numbers with which to compare.
What to Watch: The company has reported on two quarters since its IPO last June. The shares have gotten crushed both time, falling 18% and 19%, respectively. On Tuesday analysts will want to see margin improvement and gauge the company’s progress on its fulfillment operations, which was moved to New Jersey, causing a spike in expenses.
PepsiCo ( PEP ) - Reports before the open, Tuesday, Feb. 13.
Wall Street expects EPS of $1.30 per share on revenue of $19.39 billion, compared to the year-ago quarter of $1.20 per share on $19.52 billion in revenue.
What to Watch: Can revenue continue to rise? In Q3 revenue came in at $16.2 billion, missing consensus estimates of $16.3 billion. But the 1.3% year-over-year increase marked the fourth straight quarter of improving sales following eight straight quarters of declines. The company is adjusting to consumers’ need for healthier beverage choices with low salt, low sugar, and more natural ingredients.
Under Armour ( UAA ) - Reports before the open, Tuesday, Feb. 13.
Wall Street expects a breakeven quarter of $0.00 per share on revenue of $1.31 billion, compared to the year-ago quarter of earnings of 23 cents per share on $1.31 billion in revenue.
What to Watch: Sporting goods retailers and department stores are struggling to compete with Amazon. As a way to attract more shoppers, Under Armour management decided to shift from selling higher-margin apparel toward lower-margin footwear via aggressive promotions. But the company’s expenses, including investments in Direct-to-Consumer and R&D, is expected to pressure margins for this fiscal year and next.
Cisco Systems ( CSCO ) - Reports after the close, Wednesday , Feb. 14.
Wall Street expects EPS of 59 cents per share on revenue of $11.8 billion, compared to the year-ago quarter of 57 cents per share on $11.58 billion in revenue.
What to Watch: The company is still in a midst of a transformation. Cisco no longer wants to rely solely on its core routing and switching business and has made moves toward a more software-centric, subscription-based model. On Wednesday investors will want to see whether Cisco will finally guide for the next quarter and fiscal year in a way that inspires confidence it can grow the software side of the business to offset the expected decline in hardware.
Bottom Line
Despite the massive selling we’ve seen last week, the Dow, as well as the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq Composite index all ended down just a little over 5% for the week. Indeed, this correction, which began two weeks ago, has been a stomach-churning event. But it has also pushed some individual stocks toward intriguing levels not seen for some time. And if you own any of the five stocks above that are reporting this week, be prepared to deploy or re-deploy some cash.
